side_a: CC 6.1.9 The bit is set when the owner was active in this period or any of the previous three. It is not something recoverable from a sum.
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json reads=census:member:partial&last(4); over=active/owner; combine=count(owner)
note: The text has the owner compute its own four-period bit and every member recompute the count "from the two partials" of the period. The fold cell (and the CC 8.10 card) reads the last four periods of partials and counts owners, which a sum cannot give and which counts an owner once per period it reported. The window is in the bit, not in the fold. The census model README says the same as the text.

side_a: CC 4.5.13 A silent member is not in the denominator. The tally is taken over **who shows up**
side_b: CC 4.5.13 The base is the standing roster at or below the count minimum the governance policy table pins and, above it, the expected-active count
note: The fallback vote on a moderation action is counted over the members who voted on that proposal in one paragraph, and over the census base in another. The policy row moderation_action has base active and floor 1/2, and CC 6.1 calls the base "a denominator a community's rules read". With 3 of 40 expected-active members voting, 2 keep-votes carry under the first and fail under the second. The census model names the first reading (ThresholdBase = responders) as the one its invariant refuses.

note: The fabric (the node) fires the takedown notice and the `moderation:*` event on a match. note: CC 3.4.10 says the `witness` identity_type emits only log cosignatures, that the witness of `age_assurance:*` is a different thing ("Being a registered provider, authority or assessor"), and that a substrate MUST NOT accept one where another is required. CC 3.4.11 and CC 3.4.12 gate both ladders on that same identity_type. Under CC 3.4.11 a log witness may attest a person adult; under CC 3.4.10 it may not. The family model has a third rule: a delegated `infra:attest_assurance` scope.

side_a: CC 4.5.4 Belonging to the set holds no duty, so a member who has not been appointed moderates nothing.
side_b: CC 4.5.13 A founder holds the duty at zero hops and no row confers it
note: authority_set(C) is "a founder, or a key the community's consensus_protocol authorizes". The authority-set paragraph of CC 4.5.4 says belonging to it holds no duty; CC 4.5.13 and a later paragraph of CC 4.5.4 ("its zero-hop duty persists") say a founder holds the duty with no row. Read alone, the first refuses a moderation act signed by a founder nobody appointed, and locks the room for election while a founder is live; the second admits the act and never locks. CC 4.5.13 (founder's seat, "A founder is never locked out") supports the zero-hop reading; the authority-set sentence lacks the founder exception.

side_a: CC 3.3.1: `consent:state:*` rows on one subject use the same boundary fold, the latest admitted revocation's `asserted_at` putting every earlier grant out
side_b: CC 4.4.3.5.5: a revoke is terminal for the grant it names (its supersedes_id); a revoke that
note: CC 3.3.1 puts every grant at or before the latest revocation out, whichever row it named; the CC 4.4.3.5.5 read path removes only the named or withdrawn grant, so an older unnamed grant resolves to granted. Withdrawing the newest grant resurrects an older one under 4.4.3.5.5 and never under 3.3.1. The consent model pinned by the register follows CC 3.3.1.

side_a: CC 3.3.4: A widening or removal is judged at its signed instant, which its signers choose.
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.2: current = resolve_family(F, now)
note: CC 2.4 and CC 3.3.4 judge a cosigned roster event on the fold at its signed instant, a departed signer counting inside W; the CC 4.4.3.4.2 gate resolves the roster and counts signatures (and the founder role) against the roster at now. A signer who left between signing and receipt counts under one and not the other, so the same event is admitted or refused. CC 2.6.7 and the membership model support the signed instant.
